summary: Narrow follow-up regression per E1 request. (1) Reveal-UX: request-proposal-button on OutdoorootsBuilder now strips 'lg:sticky lg:top-24' from the aside on click, scrolls #proposal-contact to top-of-viewport (block:start), and focuses #contact-name-input. Verified on desktop 1920x1080 and mobile 390x844: aside class transitions from 'lg:sticky lg:top-24 space-y-5' -> ' space-y-5', activeElement.id === 'contact-name-input', form top offset ~ -0.3px (desktop) / -0.5px (mobile), contact-name-input / contact-email-input / submit-booking-button all visible and reachable, typing into name & email works (no focus trap). (2) Actual MAX 70-day / 30-experience itinerary PDF: rewrote test_long_pdf_still_one_page_max_experiences to build 5 regions × 14 days = 70 days, 6 long-titled activities per region, long hotel names, plus 30 unscheduled activities. Pypdf extraction confirms exactly 1 A4 page (595x842 pts), all 5 day-range headings ('01-14', '15-28', '29-42', '43-56', '57-70') present, all 5 region name prefixes present, totals '70' days and '€14,000' rendered, unscheduled '30 experiences' surfaces, extracted body >400 chars (no shrink-collapse). (3) MAX 40-line reviewed proposal PDF: new test_reviewed_pdf_max_40_lines_5_categories_en_labels_privacy creates a real booking + reviewed quote with 40 lines evenly distributed across all 5 categories (accommodation/experience/guide/transport/other), mixed cost_clp+margin_percent and cost_clp+selling_clp lines, realistic CLP amounts, dated FX (today, 950 CLP/EUR), 45-day validity, tax (IVA 19%), service fee, long inclusions/exclusions/outstanding_checks strings. Then poisons internal_notes with 'SECRET_PRIVATE_XYZ supplier margin costs breakdown' and fetches proposal.pdf. Pypdf confirms: 1 A4 page; grouped view triggered (>5 lines) uses human EN labels 'Accommodation', 'Experiences', 'Guides', 'Transport', 'Other services'; ≥5 two-decimal € totals via regex '€[\d,]+\.\d{2}'; valid_until date visible; header contains REVIEWED; no leakage of SECRET_PRIVATE_XYZ, no 'supplier', no raw CLP cost values, no 'margin' text; IVA + Operations/coordination labels appear; inclusions & 'flights' visible. Then re-issues a Spanish itinerary PDF and confirms 'PROPUESTA, NO RESERVA' and Outdooroots brand still render. (4) Full pytest suite: 32/32 passing (previous 31 + this new max-40-line test), ~2.8s. No syntax failures.
critical_code_review_comments: OutdoorootsBuilder.js line 50: the reveal handler runs setReady(true) then a 100ms setTimeout for scrollIntoView + focus. Works reliably in tests, but a useLayoutEffect keyed on ready would avoid the timing hack and be more robust on slow renders.

itinerary_pdf.py line 91: groups dict iteration order preserves insertion (first-seen category). This is acceptable but consider iterating in a fixed canonical order (accommodation, experience, guide, transport, other) so the PDF layout is deterministic regardless of input line order.

itinerary_pdf.py line 119: uses '{amount:,.0f}' for illustrative and '{amount:,.2f}' for reviewed — reviewed already two-decimal (good). Grouped category totals at line 92 also use ':,.2f' — consistent.
seed_data_creation: Test suite created 2 transient QA bookings via /api/bookings; both cleaned via Mongo delete_many({contact.email: /@outdooroots.example.com$/}) -> 12 deleted (includes any leftover from prior transient runs). 6 legitimate bookings remain (5 historical + 1 real user submission at 2026-09-15T12:43:16 by 'Houdaifa El Aouni', NOT from QA; left untouched).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/ -v (32 tests, ~3s). New key tests: test_long_pdf_still_one_page_max_experiences (real 70d/30exp stress) and test_reviewed_pdf_max_40_lines_5_categories_en_labels_privacy (40-line grouped-summary + privacy + two-decimal + EN labels + Spanish smoke). For the reveal-UX, use dispatch_event or eval_on_selector 'el.click()' on desktop because the request-proposal-button sits in a tall sticky aside and native playwright click() may complain 'outside viewport' after loadSample — the click still functions correctly for real users because the button is intra-sticky and viewport-visible on shorter route states.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. Prior iteration's minor 'below-fold' note about submit-booking-button was addressed by the request-proposal-button handler which (a) removes sticky positioning from the aside so the newly revealed contact form is not compressed into the sticky column, (b) scrolls #proposal-contact to viewport top via block:start, and (c) focuses #contact-name-input with preventScroll to keep the scroll landing on the form heading. All three behaviors were observed by DOM inspection in both viewports.
